standard_prerequisites.name: The criterion for an inverse system of distinguished triangles to induce a pro-isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the pro-isomorphism statement about K_n^bullet to pro-zeroness of the truncation system.

standard_prerequisites.name: The essentially constant cohomology criterion for a bounded complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces pro-zeroness of the truncation system to pro-zeroness of the individual cohomology systems.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Koszul complex of a sequence, its degree bounds and the annihilation of its cohomology by the ideal generated by the powers
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the degree range and the annihilation that the transition-map computation needs.

standard_prerequisites.name: Artin-Rees applied to an ideal and a submodule of a finite module
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the input that forces the transition map on cohomology to vanish.

core_obligations: Write down the inverse system of distinguished triangles tau_{<= -1}K_n^bullet -> K_n^bullet -> A/(f_1^m, ..., f_r^m) -> (tau_{<= -1}K_n^bullet)[1] (proof lines 27181-27187).
Apply the criterion for pro-isomorphisms of distinguished triangle systems to reduce to showing that the inverse system tau_{<= -1}K_n^bullet is pro-zero (proof lines 27188-27190).

Use that K_n^bullet has nonzero terms only in degrees -r <= i <= 0, so that by the essentially constant cohomology criterion it suffices to show H^p(K_n^bullet) is pro-zero for p <= -1, i.e. that for every n there is m >= n with H^p(K_m^bullet) -> H^p(K_n^bullet) zero (proof lines 27191-27198).

Use the Noetherian hypothesis to see each H^p(K_n^bullet) is a finite A-module, and observe that for p < 0 the map K_m^p -> K_n^p is given by a diagonal matrix with entries in the ideal (f_1^{m-n}, ..., f_r^{m-n}) (proof lines 27198-27205).
Note that H^p(K_n^bullet) is annihilated by J = (f_1^n, ..., f_r^n) and that (f_1^{m-n}, ..., f_r^{m-n}) is contained in J^t whenever m - n >= t n (proof lines 27206-27208).

Apply Artin-Rees to the ideal J and the module K_n^p with submodule the kernel of K_n^p -> K_n^{p+1} to conclude that for m large enough the image of K_m^p -> K_n^p meets that kernel inside the product J times the kernel, so the induced map on H^p is zero (proof lines 27209-27214).
difficulty_reason: In the situation of the Koszul construction, the lemma asserts that when A is Noetherian the pro-objects {K_n^bullet} and {A/(f_1^n, ..., f_r^n)} of D(A) are isomorphic, with a footnote spelling out the consequence that for every n there is m >= n such that K_m^bullet -> K_n^bullet factors through K_m^bullet -> A/(f_1^m, ..., f_r^m) (source lines 27171-27178). The proof is a genuine pro-isomorphism argument. It writes down the inverse system of distinguished triangles with truncation tau_{<= -1}K_n^bullet and reduces, via the criterion for pro-isomorphisms, to showing that the inverse system of truncations is pro-zero (proof lines 27181-27190). Using that K_n^bullet is concentrated in degrees -r to 0, it further reduces to showing H^p(K_n^bullet) is pro-zero for p <= -1 (proof lines 27191-27195). The substantive step is the Artin-Rees input: since A is Noetherian each H^p(K_n^bullet) is a finite A-module; the transition map K_m^p -> K_n^p for p < 0 is given by a diagonal matrix with entries in the ideal (f_1^{m-n}, ..., f_r^{m-n}); H^p(K_n^bullet) is annihilated by J = (f_1^n, ..., f_r^n); and since (f_1^{m-n}, ..., f_r^{m-n}) is contained in J^t once m - n >= t n, Artin-Rees applied to the ideal J and the module K_n^p with submodule the kernel of K_n^p -> K_n^{p+1} shows that for m large enough the image of K_m^p -> K_n^p meets that kernel inside J times the kernel, yielding the zero map (proof lines 27196-27214). The non-routine content is the diagonal-matrix description of the transition maps and the Artin-Rees step that makes them vanish on cohomology.
